```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
dat_prelim <- read.csv(here::here("P2/DataRaw", "PrelimData.csv"))
```

Correlations
```{r}
summary(dat_prelim)
pairs(dat_prelim)

# Correlations
cor_matrix <- cor(dat_prelim, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cor_matrix

ggplot(melt(cor_matrix), aes(Var1, Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    limits = c(-1, 1)
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank()
  ) + 
  labs(title = "Correlation heatmap",
       x = "", y = "")
```

There is a reasonable range of correlations from 0.2-0.7 based on the preliminary data, so that is what will be focused on for the power analysis. We will also look at two alpha correction strategies (based on the number of inflammatory markers or the number of outcomes of the aim 1)
```{r}
library(powertools)

r_vals <- seq(0.2, 0.5, by = 0.05)
  # Correlation range
N <- 175
  # Sample size
alpha_markers <- 0.05 / 4   
alpha_outcomes <- 0.05 / 6  
alpha_all <- 0.05 / 24
  # Alpha levels
power_results <- data.frame(
  r = r_vals,
  power_alpha_markers = sapply(r_vals, function(r)
    corr.1samp(N = N, rho0 = 0, rhoA = r, alpha = alpha_markers, sides = 2)),
  power_alpha_outcomes = sapply(r_vals, function(r)
    corr.1samp(N = N, rho0 = 0, rhoA = r, alpha = alpha_outcomes, sides = 2)),
  power_alpha_all = sapply(r_vals, function(r)
    corr.1samp(N = N, rho0 = 0, rhoA = r, alpha = alpha_all, sides = 2))
) # Power calculation

power_results
```

```{r}
r_vals <- seq(0.2, 0.7, by = 0.1)


ratios <- list(
  "50_50" = c(0.5, 0.5),
  "60_40" = c(0.6, 0.4),
  "70_30" = c(0.7, 0.3)
) # Amyloid group ratios

corr_pairs <- expand.grid(rho_low = r_vals, rho_high = r_vals)
corr_pairs <- subset(corr_pairs, rho_high > rho_low)
  # Correlation pairs where the interaction implies a difference

compute_power <- function(N1, N2, rho_low, rho_high, alpha) {
  corr.2samp(
    n1 = N1,
    n.ratio = N2/N1,
    rho1 = rho_low,
    rho2 = rho_high,
    alpha = alpha,
    sides = 2
  )
} # Power function

results_list <- list()

for (ratio_name in names(ratios)) {
  
  props <- ratios[[ratio_name]]
  N1 <- round(N * props[1])
  N2 <- N - N1
  
  tmp <- data.frame(
    rho_low  = corr_pairs$rho_low,
    rho_high = corr_pairs$rho_high,
    diff     = corr_pairs$rho_high - corr_pairs$rho_low,
    
    power_alpha_markers = mapply(
      compute_power,
      N1 = N1,
      N2 = N2,
      rho_low  = corr_pairs$rho_low,
      rho_high = corr_pairs$rho_high,
      alpha = alpha_markers
    ),
    
    power_alpha_outcomes = mapply(
      compute_power,
      N1 = N1,
      N2 = N2,
      rho_low  = corr_pairs$rho_low,
      rho_high = corr_pairs$rho_high,
      alpha = alpha_outcomes
    ),
    
    power_alpha_all = mapply(
      compute_power,
      N1 = N1,
      N2 = N2,
      rho_low  = corr_pairs$rho_low,
      rho_high = corr_pairs$rho_high,
      alpha = alpha_all
    )
  )
  
  results_list[[ratio_name]] <- tmp
}

### Example: view 50/50 split
results_list$`50_50`
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Combine all results into one data frame
plot_df <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(results_list), function(name) {
    results_list[[name]] %>% mutate(ratio = name)
  })
)

# Convert to long format
plot_long <- plot_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("power_"),
    names_to = "alpha_type",
    values_to = "power"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    alpha_type = recode(alpha_type,
      "power_alpha_markers"  = "0.05/4",
      "power_alpha_outcomes" = "0.05/6",
      "power_alpha_all"      = "0.05/24"
    ),
    power = power * 100   # convert to percent if needed
  )

# Main plot
ggplot(plot_long, aes(x = rho_high, y = power, color = alpha_type)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 75, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(rho_low ~ ratio) +
  labs(
    title = "Power vs Amyloid+ Correlation",
    x = "Amyloid+ Correlation (ρ_high)",
    y = "Power (%)",
    color = "Alpha Level"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue", "darkgreen")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```
